minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved a response to an Open Meeting Law complaint and added a verification task to its DEP I&I plan.
minutes.summary: The commission reviewed town counsel's draft response to an Open Meeting Law complaint, argued over whether to add commitments in it, and approved it. It heard two vendors (Badger/Stiles and Neptune/Ty Sales) on irrigation meter options, held officer elections, heard a carwash owner's sewer easement question, awarded a manhole remediation bid, and amended its I&I task list for the DEP.

public_comment.topic: A carwash owner asked whether the commission would allow a sewer easement across a new lot so he could split his property into three lots.
Public comment was invited at the start of the remaining business; nothing substantive from the floor was captured.

votes.motion: Approve the draft Open Meeting Law response letter prepared by town counsel.
Nominate and elect the chair for the coming year.
Vice chair election: Joan/John nominated against Carl; Carl declared vice chair with three votes.
Award the manhole remediation contract at thirteen thousand seven hundred dollars.
Insert a new task between tasks two and three to verify the effectiveness of I&I remediation already done in areas three and six.
Approve the FY18 commitment for sewer billing.

Per-unit cellular fee, a software upfront charge and meter prices were explained; confusing line items were corrected.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission took up town counsel's draft response to an Open Meeting Law complaint; the minutes record the vote on approving it as not audible.
The commission awarded the manhole remediation contract after a bid in which the engineer's estimate was higher than the low bid.
The commission added a task to its DEP I&I plan to verify that remediation already done in areas three and six worked.
Town counsel is to be asked to train the commission on the Open Meeting Law, together with a communication workshop, targeted for the 26th pending counsel's availability.
Badger/Stiles and Neptune/Ty Sales presented irrigation meter options, and a carwash owner asked about a sewer easement for splitting his property; the easement stays on the agenda.

why_it_matters: Irrigation meter choices and the I&I remediation plan affect how sewer use is measured and billed, and where sewer-system repair money is spent, so they can reach residents' sewer bills.

The Open Meeting Law training and workshop bear on how openly the commission deliberates, and the not-audible votes on the complaint response and billing commitment leave those outcomes unclear in the record.
watch_next: The 12th meeting agenda: irrigation meter policy, meter selection, the grease law notification policy, and the I&I item with consultant questions.
The training and communications workshop, aimed for the 26th at 6:30 pending counsel's availability.
